evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The perturbation metrics corroborate the claimed localization and faithfulness gains across four architectures and two datasets, independently of the internal heuristic weighting formula.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by external perturbation-based faithfulness metrics (Insertion AUC, Deletion AUC, Average Drop, Average Increase) computed from the target model's class prediction probabilities under masked inputs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system's parameters are derived analytically per image from the target model's own activations and gradients: lambda_rel from energy-weighted channel ratios, p from the fitted energy decay slope, and the LCN window from the participation ratio of gradient-weighted activations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics with standard errors and ablation experiments directly validate the core claims of improved localization precision and faithfulness across diverse architectures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is systematically benchmarked across both CNNs (DenseNet-121, ResNet-50) and Vision Transformers (ViT-B/16, DINOv2) on ImageNet and Oxford 102 Flowers using standard perturbation metrics (Insertion AUC, Deletion AUC, Average Drop, Average Increase) alongside ablations and parameter distribution analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Perturbation metrics Insertion/Deletion AUC and prediction drops corroborate the localization improvements across multiple models and datasets independently of the heuristic weighting formula.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard external perturbation-based faithfulness metrics (Insertion AUC, Deletion AUC, Average Drop, and Average Increase) evaluated on target model class prediction probabilities.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Internal per-image analytical calculations based on network activations and gradients (energy ratio lambda_rel, slope-derived power p, and participation-ratio window size).

primary.limitations: The authors document the increased computational footprint from second-order Hessian backward passes, higher variance on certain CNN curvature distributions, and less compact localization on complex multi-object or cluttered scenes.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is mathematically fully defined and unambiguous, specifying closed-form formulations for curvature modulation, geometric mean ratio balancing, participation-ratio window sizing, and knee-point soft masking without learned parameter fitting or external heuristics.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents an adequately scoped, well-formalized post-hoc explainability method backed by rigorous empirical benchmarks on standard vision datasets and models, extensive ablation studies, and clear reporting of methodological boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ADAPT-CAM, a post-hoc class activation mapping framework that dynamically computes per-image parameters using first-order gradient energy, second-order curvature modulation, adaptive local contrast normalization, and knee-guided soft channel selection.
